summary: Wenatchee National Forest lookout near Mission Ridge: a 1931 cab, a 1940 pole tower, and a 1973 removal. One concrete footing remains.

facts.design: 18-foot pole tower with L-4 cab (1940 to 1973)
facts.status_note: Tower came down in 1973; one concrete footing and some eyebolts remain.

access.note: Forest Road 9712 has a locked gate and is closed in winter.

visit.trail_note: Under one mile with 307 feet of elevation gain, per WillhiteWeb.

events.note: L-5 cab, at ground level per WillhiteWeb
Two CCC workers from Camp Icicle posted at the emergency lookout, per the Wenatchee Daily World (report of June 4, 1935)
August 1, 1935: a Squilichuck rancher reported a fire by phone; the call was relayed to the Wenatchee district fireman, and the lookouts could not see smoke at the place indicated
18-foot pole tower with L-4 cab replaced the L-5 cab
Observers listed from 1947 (Don Wehmeyer) to 1963 (Dave Griffith)
FFLOS says removed; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says the tower was removed in 1973; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say it was destroyed. The story reports both words and does not choose one.
WillhiteWeb's photo caption calls a 'Second Beehive Lookout' a 1963 structure. FFLOS, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb's own text date the replacement to 1940. The story uses 1940.

sources.title: Beehive Mountain - Mission Ridge Ski Area

notes_for_editor: The core timeline (1931 cab, 1940 pole tower, 1973 end) agrees across firetower.org, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb. Open points: removed versus destroyed, and the 1963 'Second Beehive Lookout' caption. The gate and winter closure come from a 2013-era SummitPost trip report, so check the road status before publishing. The brief's kind 'tower' fits the 1940 structure.
